#3125. Creative Media (CMCT) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Multifamily and hotel gains drove results as asset sales came under review

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Creative Media & Community Trust Corporation (CMCT +6.61%) reported a 55% increase in total segment net operating income during the third quarter, driven by performance gains in multifamily, office, and hotel assets. Management stated that the company remains focused on improving funds from operations, strengthening the balance sheet, and exploring strategic asset sales to narrow the gap between share price and portfolio value. The company has reduced its corporate debt to $27.1 million while continuing to fund renovations and leasing initiatives. Management indicated that fundamental recovery in the Bay Area multifamily market has led to record-high rent growth and declining vacancy rates.

Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Creative Media & Community Trust Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] Please note today's event is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Steve Altebrando. Please go ahead.

Stephen Altebrando: Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us. My name is Steve Altebrando, the portfolio oversight for CMCT. Also on the call today are David Thompson, our Chief Executive Officer; and Brandon Hill, our Chief Financial Officer. This call is being webcast and will be temporarily archived on the Investor Relations section of our website, where you can also find our earnings release. Our earnings release includes a reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures discussed during today's call. During this call, we will make forward-looking statements. These forward-looking statements are based on the beliefs of assumptions made by and information currently available to us.

Our actual results will be affected by known and unknown risks, trends and uncertainties and other factors that are beyond our control or ability to predict. Although we believe that our assumptions are reasonable, they are not guarantees of future performance and some will prove to be incorrect. Therefore, our actual future results can be expected to differ from our expectations, and those differences may be material. For a more detailed description of potential risks, please refer to our SEC filings, which can be found in the Investor Relations section of our website. With that, I'll turn the call over to David Thompson.

David Thompson: Thanks, Steve. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. In prior quarters, we have been highlighting that operating trends were improving across the multifamily portfolio, the Los Angeles and Austin office assets and the company's one hotel asset. We are pleased that this improvement has continued. Our third quarter segment net operating income increased 55% from the same period in 2025. In the multifamily segment, our NOI increased 169% year-over-year. Same-store multifamily occupancy reached 95% as of September 30, 2026, an increase of 970 basis points from a year ago. Approximately 78% of our multifamily units are located in the Bay Area, where leasing demand has continued to improve.

In-place rents at our Bay Area multifamily properties are approximately 17% below current asking rents, providing a meaningful opportunity for continued growth as new leases roll to market. In the Office segment, NOI increased 15.8% to $5.8 million from $5 million last year, primarily due to improved performance at our Wilshire office assets. We executed 59,400 square feet of leases in the quarter and have an active pipeline. In the hotel segment, our property in Sacramento also delivered improved operating performance with NOI increasing 234% year-over-year following the completion of recent renovations. Looking ahead, we believe the property is well positioned for continued NOI growth, supported by strong group booking activity.

Group room bookings for 2027 are currently up more than 20% compared to this time last year. Overall, we're encouraged by the continued improvement we're seeing across each of our operating segments, and we believe we are positioned to continue to grow our FFO. We remain focused on 3 strategic priorities: first, improving our funds from operations. In the third quarter, our core FFO improved by $6.7 million compared to the third quarter of last year. We continue to see operating trends strengthening across our multifamily portfolio, our Los Angeles and Austin office assets and at our hotel asset in Sacramento. These improvements are translating into stronger operating results, and we believe there is an opportunity for continued growth.

Second, we continue to strengthen our balance sheet while still funding critical growth initiatives, including office leasing and our hotel renovations. We are actively working on 3 asset-level refinancings. Since September of 2024, we have completed financings on 9 assets, fully retired our recourse credit facility, sold our lending business and redeemed approximately $398.9 million of the company's preferred stock in exchange for shares of common stock. As a result of these efforts, we now have just $27.1 million of corporate debt, which does not mature until 2035. Third, we continue to explore additional asset sales. We are currently marketing several real estate assets for sale.

We believe executing on this strategy will further strengthen our balance sheet while also help close what we view as the significant gap between our current share price and the intrinsic value of the portfolio. With that, I'll turn the call over to Steve to provide more color on our refinancing activities and the property level performance in the quarter.

Stephen Altebrando: Thanks, David. The actions we've taken over the past several quarters have significantly improved our balance sheet, and we believe will improve our funds from operations. We are positioned to benefit from improving fundamentals, particularly in our multifamily assets in the Bay Area. Today, CMCT owns 621 residential units across 2 premier Class A assets in the market. We continue to benefit from the positive momentum of the recovery in the Bay Area, which has been bolstered by growth in AI-related employment and investment. In San Francisco, multifamily rents increased by approximately 13% in the third quarter after increasing approximately 6% in 2025. The rent growth represents a 25-year high.

And vacancy has declined to 3.6%, which is a 25-year low. In Oakland, rent growth was 10.8% in the third quarter, also the highest rate of growth in 25-plus years. Vacancy declined to 6% at the end of the third quarter, down from a peak of approximately 17.8% in 2021. Despite the significant rent growth in the Oakland market, rents are still only around 2019 levels. The market has now largely absorbed the significant amount of supply that was added from 2018 through 2022. Future supply growth in both markets remains very low, and we anticipate that will remain low for the foreseeable future, given the elevated cost of construction.

At the end of the third quarter, occupancy at CMCT's multifamily properties increased to 96%, representing an improvement of 1,130 basis points compared to the end of the third quarter last year. We have seen concessions in the market normalize. And at the end of the third quarter of '26, our in-place rents were approximately 17% below our current asking rents. This should support solid growth in the future. Turning to Los Angeles. We have made solid progress across our 2 new L.A. multifamily assets. At 701 South Hudson, our partial office-to-residential conversion is now 95.6% occupied. We continue to work on predevelopment for the 50 additional units we are entitled to build on the adjacent surface lot.

We anticipate having the option to start this project next year. At 1915 Park, our ground-up development at Echo Park, we achieved 66.7% leased at the quarter end. This 36-unit project delivered in the fourth quarter of '25 and is located in a highly desirable, walkable submarket with significant dining and entertainment options. Including our joint ventures, we now have 5 operating multifamily assets. Turning to the Office segment. We executed approximately 59,000 square feet of leases in the third quarter. We are seeing steady leasing interest at the few assets where we have some vacancy in L.A. and Austin.

Excluding the company's Oakland office asset, our lease percentage stood at 85.2% at the end of the third quarter, representing a decline of 140 basis points year-over-year. Finally, in our hotel segment, we have substantially completed the renovation of the property's public spaces following the full renovation of all 505 guest rooms. This marks the first comprehensive renovation of the asset since its acquisition in 2008 and positions the hotel well for improved performance going forward. As David mentioned, the property has seen strong group bookings, which are up more than 20% for 2027 compared to this time last year.

We are also evaluating an opportunity to add 8 new guest rooms by converting currently underutilized space, which we believe would be highly accretive. Turning to financing. We are working to refinance our mortgages on our hotel asset and our 2 Bay Area multifamily assets. At the hotel, with the renovation now substantially complete, we believe there's an opportunity to both increase the loan balance and reduce the borrowing spread. Finally, at our Oakland office property, our nonrecourse mortgage matured in early July. We elected not to invest the additional capital in the asset that would have been required to refinance the mortgage. We continue to engage with the servicer on a long-term resolution.

While CMCT has not made any contributions to the asset since the loan matured in July, the asset impacted our core FFO by $1.6 million in the quarter because we are accruing a stepped-up interest rate on the mortgage. With that, I'll turn it to Brandon.

Brandon Hill: Thank you, Steve. Good afternoon. I'm going to spend a few minutes going over the comparative financial highlights for the third quarter of 2026 versus the third quarter of 2025, starting with our segment NOI, which was $10.8 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $7 million in the prior year comparable period.

Loss from unconsolidated entities was $123,000 in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $697,000 in the prior year comparable period, with the decrease primarily driven by fair value adjustments to real estate at our unconsolidated office entities and our unconsolidated multifamily entities and an increase in net income at one of our unconsolidated office entities for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the prior year comparable period. Excluding loss from unconsolidated entities, segment NOI was $10.9 million in Q3 2026 compared to $7.7 million in Q3 2025.

Broken down by segment, the increase in segment NOI of approximately $3.8 million was driven by an increase of $2 million from our hotel property, $1.3 million from our multifamily properties and $793,000 from our office properties, partially offset by a decrease of $314,000 due to the sale of our Lending segment during Q1 2026. Our hotel segment NOI for Q3 2026 was $2.8 million versus $850,000 in Q3 2025. The increase was primarily driven by increased occupancy, which resulted in increased room revenues and food and beverage revenues. These increases were partially offset by higher room expenses and food and beverage expenses for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the prior year comparable period.

Our multifamily segment net operating income increased to $2.1 million for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $792,000 for the same period in 2025, primarily driven by increases in occupancy and monthly rent per occupied unit, net of rent concessions, coupled with a decrease in real estate taxes at our multifamily properties in Oakland. As of September 30, 2026, our same-store multifamily portfolio was 95% occupied compared to 85.3% as of September 30, 2025. Our office segment NOI for Q3 2026 was $5.8 million versus $5 million in Q3 2025.

The increase was primarily driven by fair value adjustments to real estate and an increase in net income at one of our unconsolidated office entities during Q3 2026, higher rental revenue at our office properties in Los Angeles and San Francisco as well as a decrease in operating expenses at our office property in Oakland, driven by lower utility-related expenses. These increases were partially offset by lower rental and tenant reimbursement revenue at our office property in Oakland as well as lower tenant reimbursement revenue at our office property in Beverly Hills during Q3 2026 compared to the prior year period.

Below the segment NOI line, we incurred $8 million of impairment charges during Q3 2026 due to impairment recognized in connection with office properties in Austin and San Francisco. In addition, interest expense not allocated to our operating segments increased $816,000 and provision for income taxes increased $754,000, respectively, compared to the prior year period. Our FFO was negative $4 million or negative $1.30 per diluted share compared to negative $11.1 million or negative $1,390.50 per diluted share in the prior year comparable period.

The increase in FFO was primarily attributable to a decrease in redeemable preferred stock dividends of $4.3 million and an increase of $3.8 million in segment net operating income, partially offset by an increase in interest expense not allocated to our operating segments of $816,000 and a higher provision for income taxes of $754,000. Our core FFO was negative $3.8 million or negative $1.26 per diluted share compared to negative $10.5 million or negative $1,315.75 per diluted share in the prior year comparable period. The increase in core FFO is primarily attributable to the aforementioned changes in FFO. With that, we can open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] And today's first question comes from David Storms at Stonegate Capital.

David Storms: I want to start -- you mentioned you have several assets marketed for sale. Just hoping you could give us some perspective on that pipeline. And maybe what you're seeing in terms of higher interest and pricing. Have market conditions improved enough to maybe start narrowing that gap?

Stephen Altebrando: Yes. So I could take that. So we are marketing for sale currently several assets, both -- including both office and residential and are moving forward with that process. I think from the market's perspective right now, I mean, we generally have -- I think the biggest component being the rising 10-year. So I think for -- specifically to office, which I think is a little bit less impacted by that, you're clearly seeing office market recover and leasing activity is picking up. But I think there's still generally somewhat of a wide bid-ask spread when it comes to cap rate. So I think those are kind of the key dynamics, what you're seeing on the office side.

And the multifamily, I think it is very much rate-driven. I think our assets specifically on the multifamily side are newer vintage, and for most of them, still ramping up. So do have some rent growth and reduced concessions, so -- which takes on a little bit of its own dynamic as well. But overall, I would say the capital markets are not terrific because of where the yields are moving. But we, from our perspective, think it's very important for us to clean -- to basically generate some more liquidity so we can more effectively manage the preferred redemptions that we're seeing.

David Storms: Understood. That makes sense. If I could just ask one follow-up, maybe sticking with the multifamily. You mentioned the ramping up. It was also mentioned that current rents are about 17% below the current asking rents. I guess how should we think about the catch-up here in this gap? And would that gap maybe persist assuming the market continues to rebound and rents continue to climb? Maybe any distinction on that interplay would be very helpful.

Stephen Altebrando: Yes. The good news is that we've -- particularly in the Bay Area, rents have increased pretty dramatically and are continuing to grow. So that's great news for us. That has increased the mark-to-market opportunity. It does mean as that spread has widened that it take a little bit more time to get all the rents to market. I think from -- when you're thinking of an asset that on average is 17% below mark-to-market, that's probably -- could take you a couple of years to get those 2 assets fully to market. So I think that's the timeline about that we're thinking of.

#3124. Pixel users are getting a major Android Auto update – and it rivals Siri AI

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android

More phones are getting Gemini Intelligence, but only Pixel users can access it in a new way.

Gemini Intelligence is spreading beyond the Google Pixel 11 lineup to the Pixel 10, the upcoming Motorola Signature 27, and several of Samsung’s Galaxy foldables and flagship phones.

Though Google often offers its most upgraded features to other Android phone manufacturers, there are some features that are Pixel-exclusive or come to Pixel users first. This time, Gemini Intelligence is coming to Android Auto, but only for eligible Pixel users.

Also: I’m an Android Auto ride or die – but Apple CarPlay beats it on these 3 features

Google’s blog post states that Pixel users with Gemini Intelligence can expect it to gather information from their apps and surface it to their car’s infotainment screen. Google’s example is that if a friend texts you asking where you’re meeting for Pilates, Gemini Intelligence can find the correct confirmation email and offer to send it with one tap.

To access Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto, the Gemini app and subsequent setup are required; it’s available in select countries to users aged 18 and older, and feature availability will vary.

With more context about your messages, emails, and calendar events, a more capable assistant can complete cross-app tasks while driving, such as “remind me to buy mom a birthday card before her birthday” or “which route to my dentist appointment will be the fastest?” I often use Siri AI in CarPlay for tasks like these, and Gemini operates the same way. However, these tasks require user input first; what makes an AI assistant in in-car software great is when it suggests tasks before you ask for them.

Siri suggests to me when I should leave my house for an upcoming event in my calendar, such as a dinner reservation, flight, or doctor’s appointment, based on traffic conditions. It looks like Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto will offer the same assistance. I’ve reached out to Google to confirm, and will update this article if I get a response.

Also: 4 wireless Android Auto adapters we recommend (and they’re cheap)

I find Siri’s upgraded capabilities most useful when I have a busy day and heavy Atlanta traffic is thrown in the mix. Sometimes people need information about where to meet up, but I don’t remember the exact name of the location or which street it’s on. It’s difficult to search through my old messages or emails while staying alert to crazed drivers on the interstate, so a smarter AI assistant comes in handy.

Though Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto is reserved for Pixel users, the upgrade follows a series of improvements Google has rolled out to its in-car software. Non-Pixel Android phones and Android phones without Gemini Intelligence can use Personal Intelligence, which connects Gemini across your Google Maps, Photos, or Gmail data.

Personal Intelligence users can ask Gemini to navigate to a restaurant with a specific cuisine or vibe, or search their photos to find a car wash they photographed last week. Gemini Intelligence is more proactive and expansive, drawing on more sensitive data from your phone, such as messages, while Personal Intelligence relies solely on data from your Google services.

#3123. Before Grand Theft Auto 6, CNET Staff Relive Their Favorite GTA Moments

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The Grand Theft Auto series is almost 30 years old. Here are some of our favorite memorable moments down the years.

Rockstar Games is set to release Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday, Nov. 19, with both PlayStation and Xbox saying it’s the most preordered game in the history of either platform’s digital storefront. Given the 13 years of buildup and hype surrounding the game, that’s perhaps not surprising.

Though the series has evolved over time, Grand Theft Auto has been a pop culture behemoth since its inception in 1997, thanks to its biting satire, complex storylines and cinematic gameplay.

As we get our consoles ready for Grand Theft Auto 6, CNET staffers are looking back at some standout moments from the storied gaming franchise. From the original Grand Theft Auto to the streets of San Andreas and beyond, here are some of our favorite GTA memories.

Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is still my favorite GTA game.

I have so many memories of playing Grand Theft Auto games at an age some might call “too young.” I’d go over a friend’s house and we’d boot up Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas on his PlayStation 2 and do whatever we wanted. It wasn’t until later that I found out there were missions to accomplish. And the funniest part for me was failing the mission Wrong Side of the Tracks in San Andreas. The character Big Smoke would utter the iconic line, “All we had to do was follow the damn train, CJ!” That line is funny, goofy and a good reminder that beneath the guns and violence, these are inherently silly, unserious games.

I still quote the policemen from GTA London 1969 who yell, “Stop right there! Oi!” My friends and I in college would play it hotseat-style on my ancient laptop, and the cockney coppers became a meme (or “banter” as we called it back then, onions hanging from our belts as was the fashion).

I’ll say walking out of Blockbuster with a copy of GTA: Vice City as a teen whose most hard-core games before that were maybe Twisted Metal and Shivers 2 made me feel like a rock star. Tearing across the city, blowing red lights and running over onlookers was an absolute thrill, especially since my friends and I didn’t even have our learner’s permits yet.

The moment that sticks with me the most, however, was the infamous private dance scene in the Pole Position mission. I was playing over a long weekend at my best friend’s house, taking turns at the wheel, when we finally got to the scandalous part we’d read about on the internet. But instead of titillated, she and I were reduced to fits of giggles as the pixelated private dancer blockily gyrated on screen. And – sorry to our parents – after regaining composure, we immediately got to copying the unsultry choreo and teaching it to our friends. These moves would be busted out at the most opportune moments, even when we got old enough to go to real clubs. Sadly, it’s never earned us as much as a free drink.

Nothing says blowing off steam like blowing up a few cars.

When GTA 5 came out in 2013, I had just graduated from college, moved back home with my parents and had no idea what to do with my life. So I waited several hours in line at my local GameStop, along with hundreds of other people, to be the first to get the game. I rushed back home and played for an irresponsible amount of time. There was something comforting about having an entire world to explore when I felt stuck in my own. Mostly, though, I made life worse for the people of Los Santos. My degree wasn’t opening many doors, but carjacking was.

Forget the explosion-packed heists or the bullet-riddled car chases around city streets; my favorite GTA moment is when I discovered just how vast the GTA 5 map was and how much of it I could explore on foot. Or by helicopter.

GTA 5’s map was considered massive when it launched, and while I thoroughly enjoyed playing through the game’s actual storylines, I spent just as much time (if not more) simply seeing what’s out there beyond the expected play zones.

The GTA 6 map is apparently at least twice the size of that of GTA 5, and I’m super hyped to settle into hour after hour of serene exploration of a whole new landscape.

For more on GTA 6, here’s what we know about the game and how to prep your console for the massive file size.

#3122. Oura Ring users may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Oura's acquisition of Counsel Health could signal a new dawn for digital care.

Oura has entered into an agreement to acquire AI primary care company Counsel Health for $625 million. The acquisition of Counsel Health, which was already a partner in the Oura app, will give users access to Counsel’s in-house physicians and 24/7 medical AI.

The Oura Ring has evolved from its beginnings as a sleep tracker to what its CEO, Tom Hale, calls “a doctor in your pocket.” The company has its sights set on making the device a continuous medical companion, and Counsel’s acquisition is one way it’s furthering that mission.

Oura employs its 24/7 health monitoring to recognize potential deviations from a user’s biometric baseline, and the partnership will build on those capabilities by adding more clinical guidance through Counsel Health.

The partnership will also connect members with Counsel Health’s medical AI and in-house physicians to address timely health problems, support, or “prescriptions for episodic health conditions,” the press release said. The acquisition offers specialty and chronic care for chronic conditions, like reproductive, aging, and cardiometabolic-related conditions.

“Oura tells members what’s happening in their bodies, and Counsel helps them act on it. This combination expands our addressable market and deepens the value we deliver to every member,” David Shuman, executive chairman of Oura, said in a press release.

This is the third acquisition Oura has made this year, following its acquisition of Galen AI, a conversational and personal health platform that connects smart ring data to medical records, and Doublepoint AI, an AI‑driven, biometric and gesture recognition company that could add voice or gesture controls to Oura’s next smart ring.

Also: Before you buy a smart ring, consider what you’re giving up

The Counsel Health deal is expected to close by the end of the year. It’s unknown whether access to Counsel Health physicians or the 24/7 medical AI will be included in an Oura app subscription.

Tech companies have a growing appetite for health tech startups. Last year, Samsung announced a similar acquisition of Xealth, a care platform that connects more than 500 hospitals with 70 digital health centers. The acquisition, according to Samsung VP of digital health Praveen Raja, furthers Samsung’s mission to connect the healthcare landscape, from symptom detection to care provider connection.

One of the Oura Ring’s superpowers is its ability to detect developing illnesses or deviations from my biometric baseline (a spiked resting heart rate, a higher body temperature) before I feel those symptoms. I’ve written about how my Oura Ring detected an illness earlier this year, one day before I began to feel sick.

Also: I should’ve listened to my Oura Ring when it warned me about my health

When Oura has flagged these concerns to me, I take them seriously, even as my care provider — to whom I show this data — may shrug them off. The Counsel Health acquisition enables medical AI and in-house physicians to contextualize your biometrics when you are sick or managing a chronic condition.

Will this acquisition help ease the demand for urgent care clinics? As a regular visitor to and hater of my Brooklyn CityMD, I hope so. It is notoriously difficult to get a same-day, in-person appointment with a primary care provider in New York because of high demand and a stretched-thin healthcare system, which often leaves urgent care as the only in-person option for patients.

The press release says that users could ask physicians for prescriptions. I’m thinking that if I get another bad cold this winter, I could go to my Oura app for help and symptom management instead of CityMD. Making a physician readily available to Oura users could, in theory, reduce dependence on primary or urgent care providers.

#3121. No, the World Won’t Shut Down on Nov. 17. What the Blackout Rumors Get Wrong

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

There'll be an Emergency Alert System test on that date, but predictions that a catastrophe is coming are likely false, experts said.

As global conspiracy theories go, this is a juicy one.

On Tuesday, Nov. 17, at around 2:20 p.m. ET, the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the Federal Communications Commission are planning a test of the Emergency Alert System. That’s when all hell is supposed to break loose. At least, that’s what you might believe if you only rely on social media.

Coming just days after an abrupt and disruptive government-ordered shutdown of air travel in the US and technical issues that caused an unwelcome outage of widely used Microsoft workplace software, the test will be happening in an atmosphere of heightened anxiety.

Videos across Facebook, Instagram and TikTok have floated the theory that this emergency test signals a catastrophe is coming, potentially stemming from a cyberattack or a digital disruption that could knock out electricity, internet and other services. Many have started scrambling to buy emergency supplies, pointing to the need for a 90-day stockpile of food, water, cash and essential medicines in case hackers wipe out bank accounts and shut down the web.

Similar rumors have spread globally, as the governments of France, the UK and Canada have put renewed attention on the importance of households being able to survive a potential weather-related crisis or technological disaster.

How extreme have the conspiracy theories gotten? Some have cited a 2023 Simpsons episode as proof, which referenced a massive Nov. 17 blackout in Lisa’s future, even though it didn’t mention a year.

For Gen Xers and Boomers, this panic could feel familiar. Leading up to the year 2000, there were fears that a potential computer-related disaster, known as Y2K, would cause widespread chaos and disruption, based on the belief that older digital systems couldn’t handle the calendar change. The new year ended with only minor glitches, thanks to a significant global effort to update computer systems to avoid the bug.

Before we delve into the suspicions, let’s start with a bit of debunking: CNET spoke with multiple experts in disaster preparedness and cyberattacks, who all cautioned against letting our guard down. But remember that no federal agency or institution has mentioned a blackout. Unless hackers decide to take advantage of the hysteria already generated, there’s no reason to think Nov. 17 is any riskier than any other date.

Richard Mariano, a protective intelligence expert at Kronus Intelligence, who spent nearly three decades with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, said that people share all sorts of things that get picked up and go viral. “Then it creates panic where panic is not necessary,” he said.

Mariano said too many people are spreading fear rather than seeking the truth. “On every one of these social media posts that is suspect or has some form of conspiratorial edge to them: source it, source it, source it.”

Next week’s nationwide Emergency Alert System, or EAS, is similar to the public tests Americans have experienced since 1963, when the Emergency Broadcast System replaced an older radio-based warning system called CONELRAD. In 1997, the Emergency Broadcast System was replaced by the EAS, part of FEMA’s Integrated Public Alert and Warning System, which broadcasts emergency alerts to any wireless device in the country, including phones, radios and televisions. The system was designed for the president to communicate with US households within 10 minutes of a national emergency.

The Nov. 17 test will consist of a nationwide EAS message issued by FEMA, noting that no public action is required. The test will include standard alert tones to support accessibility for those who are deaf or hard of hearing and should last about a minute. This time around, wireless emergency alerts will not be triggered on mobile phones, so don’t expect a notification on your cellphone. After the alert, programming should resume as normal on TV, radio and other broadcast channels.

Many equate the emergency system with threats of nuclear war, but it could also be used to alert people to a major weather event, a national cyberattack or even AMBER alerts at the local level (without a presidential message). So it’s natural there might be some anxiety.

“With this event simulating an activation of an emergency notification system, it would be a logical next step to worry about what happens if something bad happens during that test,” said Robby Winchester, chief global professional services officer at SpecterOps, a Virginia-based security company,

But, all in all, these system tests are routine. Local stations conduct a weekly test, and federal law requires a nationwide EAS test every three years. In addition to helping people get used to responding to alerts, the tests also allow the government to identify potential technical or operational issues it needs to fix before an actual emergency alert.FEMA has a backup date of Dec. 3 in case it can’t perform it on Nov. 17 — which could happen if the agency is dealing with a real emergency or if there are technical issues. Representatives from the FCC and FEMA did not respond to a request for comment.

Another factor that helped spark conspiracy theories was a Pentagon order requiring military bases to stock enough supplies for 90 days without outside support. Dubbed “Fortress America,” the initiative memo (PDF) was released in late September but got more attention as the November date approached.

The timing of that memo coincided with the UK launching a campaign on Oct. 22 called Be Ready, urging citizens to keep enough supplies (PDF) such as water, food, medical kits and pet products to last at least three days. Other countries, including Japan, Sweden and about a dozen more, are also urging citizens to prepare for emergencies.

Still, the blackout rumor isn’t solely driven by government communications. Heightened global instability over the past few months has also played a major role. Just in the last month, the Federal Aviation Administration called a nationwide ground stop on all departing flights; a major Microsoft Outlook outage kept millions of people from working; PHP vulnerabilities exposed websites to hacking; and cyberattacks have targeted supermarket fridges and freezers across Europe.

On the financial side, Nvidia’s CEO scandal led to a stock plunge and fears of an AI bust, while Paraguay just experienced a major digital bank collapse that froze millions of accounts. The ongoing wars in Iran and Ukraine have sparked national security concerns, and floods in Nepal and fires in Indonesia demonstrate the increased dangers of climate change.

Though there’s never been a nationwide power outage in the US (several regional outages have been triggered by overloaded lines and software bugs), The New York Times reports that there’s still no comprehensive plan for what to do if the country goes completely dark.

All the online chatter surrounding Nov. 17 has raised concerns that warnings of a potential cyberattack might inadvertently trigger one.

Winchester said that even though there’s no specific information indicating an imminent crisis, “it is common for attackers to use current events of all types to help with achieving successful attacks.” The upside? If people are being spurred by government notices and their anxiety over global instability to prepare emergency supplies, it could actually help in the event of a real threat or disaster.

Regardless of whether you buy into the Nov. 17 conspiracy theories, it doesn’t hurt to have some supplies at the ready, which could be useful in the event of a digital disruption or weather event, even if it doesn’t involve nuclear weapons or hackers.

“We live in a world where there are many threats to our communities, our families and ourselves,” said Philip Farina, chief advisor for Risky Business and a federal law enforcement veteran. “Understanding the basics of self-reliance is important. Even preparing for a residential fire, which is very common, can help to save lives and protect us better.”

You don’t need to buy enough for 90 days off the grid (and most of us can’t afford that), but it’s recommended that families have at least three days’ worth of food and supplies. Some of the basics listed on Ready.gov’s Build a Kit page include:

While warnings from governments can spark panic and distrust, they can be beneficial at a time when we’re so reliant on the internet and cell service, which can be easily disrupted. Mariano said it’s worth being prepared in the “old-fashioned ways.”

#3119. Google Fi now switches between the best mobile networks automatically – how it works

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Home & Office > Networking > Mobile Carriers

Pixel users also get a bonus Wi-Fi upgrade. Here's what to know.

From left to right: Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8, Google Pixel 11, Google Pixel 11 Pro XL.

Google Fi wireless customers with Pixel phones just got a serious upgrade to their mobile and Wi-Fi connections for free.

Google has announced two new “super network” connection features for Fi Wireless: one that automatically switches between two of the largest 5G cellular networks, and another that automatically connects to premium Wi-Fi in millions of locations without you needing to log in.

The features are rolling out today for Pixel 9 phones and newer models on every Google Fi plan. If you’re not a current Fi customer, you can sign up for a free seven-day trial to test it alongside your current carrier.

Here’s how the new mobile connection feature works: if your main connection slows or becomes unstable, Fi will automatically move to a secondary connection. This not only means you’ll have the fastest option when your connection is good, but you’ll have fewer dead zones when service is limited.

Also: I compared Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T 5G coverage on a road trip – and the winner surprised me

The feature will run on MEP (Multiple Enabled Profiles) technology, which allows a single eSIM chip to host and run multiple SIM profiles simultaneously. Footnotes in Google’s release note that you’ll need to have “any non-Fi SIMs disabled.”

Google Fi originally offered automatic switching between two networks when the service debuted a decade ago, but it was between Sprint and T-Mobile, which merged in 2020. Google didn’t reveal what the “two of America’s best 5G cellular networks” were, but ZDNET has reached out to ask. The service usually runs on T-Mobile. Along with T-Mobile, the three biggest carriers are AT&T and Verizon, so it’s likely the second carrier is one of those.

In addition to a mobile connection upgrade, users are getting better Wi-Fi, too. Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ will automatically connect you to faster Wi-Fi in millions of locations like airports and malls (Google defines “faster” as two times better reliability and 30% improved latency compared to normal Google Fi cellular networks) without you having to log in or head to your settings. These connections will be automatically encrypted, Google said, keeping your online activity safe.

Also: 6 default Pixel 11 settings I changed that made a big difference – and why

This feature is also coming to Samsung phones running One UI 9 or higher and select modern Motorola phones.

Both of these features, Google explained, are available internationally and are included on Unlimited Premium and Flexible plans at no extra cost.
