Our competitive advantages in technology and product quality are becoming increasingly evident in international markets, with pre-vehicle (sic) [ per-vehicle ] profit contribution substantially higher than in the domestic market. We're rolling out multiple models, including the GX, G9L and MONA L05 across global markets and our order backlog is growing rapidly. In key markets such as Australia and the U.K., we're investing more resources in building locally operated subsidiaries. This approach has been well received by dealers and customers, driving faster expansion of our sales network and market share. We're also ramping up our production capacity in Europe and other overseas markets.

By deepening our partnerships with global automotive industry and supply chain partners, we can better meet customer expectations and regulatory requirements. Looking ahead to 2027, I believe XPeng will sustain robust growth and significantly outperform the broader industry. We plan to launch multiple new models and facelift versions to expand our product portfolio and grow our market share in China and overseas. In the domestic market, we will expand our sales network through more diverse high-quality formats, bringing XPeng series vehicles, MONA series and our robots to cover more regional markets. We'll also offer more targeted products and services to better address diverse customer needs.

In international markets, we expect our sales network to exceed 1,000 stores, supporting more than a doubling of overseas sales compared with 2026. Our international business will account for a substantially higher share of total vehicle sales and revenue and make a meaningful profit. Our goal is that XPeng continues to lead the deployment and commercialization of autonomous driving technologies in China and around the world. In the third quarter, we rolled out a new version of the second-generation VLA to users in China, including VLA Lite for Max owners. User experience and satisfaction have improved markedly.

During the Paris Motor Show in October, XPeng was the only Chinese automaker to partner with the event organizer to offer autonomous driving testing experiences, competing head-to-head with another international automaker. Despite complex road conditions in Central Paris and traffic rules different from those in China, XPeng's NGP successfully navigated the Arc de Triomphe roundabout. We expect to be among the first batch to obtain regulatory approval in the EU in 2027, enabling us to take the lead in deploying urban ADAS in Europe. We have been particularly encouraged by overseas customers' keen interest in our AI-powered ADAS and smart cockpit technologies.

Even before relevant local regulations are in place, a sizable portion of customers have already chosen the premium Ultra version. I believe the rollout of VLA and VLM will give XPeng a powerful competitive differentiator globally, driving higher sales volumes and average selling prices. It will also play a pivotal role in building XPeng into a global technology brand. More importantly, our ultimate goal for XPeng NGP is to achieve Level 4 autonomous driving capabilities in mass-produced vehicles for consumers. I believe the Level 4 experience will create highly sticky demand for paid autonomous driving capabilities in the consumer market. XPeng's Robotaxi business has taken a major step toward commercial operations.

We have recently been granted approval to conduct intelligent connected vehicle demonstration operations to carry out L4 Robotaxi demonstrations across Guangzhou. We have officially launched XPENG YOYO as our Robotaxi service brand. Starting in the fourth quarter of this year, we plan to deploy a replicable product and service model in Guangzhou and begin offering end-to-end solutions to global partners next year. As our technical and operational capabilities continue to advance, I believe XPENG YOYO will begin scaling the operations in 2028, starting with overseas markets. L4 autonomous driving will make mobility safer and more convenient while generating higher revenue from hardware and software sales, services and revenue sharing from operations.

Our next-generation humanoid robot is accelerating toward the hardware mass production by year-end. In September, we put our first automated production line for advanced general-purpose humanoid robots into operation. The production line has an automation rate of over 80% across core manufacturing processes and is designed to support mass production at automotive grade quality standards. We have also finished signing supplier nomination agreements with our suppliers. Leading component manufacturers have provided active support to ramp up production. Our full-stack in-house R&D capabilities featuring deep integration of hardware and software are complemented by years of experience in manufacturing and supply chain management.

Together, these strengths give me confidence that XPeng's humanoid robots will be industry-leading in design, quality, production efficiency and cost competitiveness. Advanced intelligence is XPENG IRON's greatest competitive advantage. We would like to do away with remotes. We want to operate without the rules dictated by preset software. IRON can recognize multiple people and remember their identities. When interacting with people, it can observe and think in real time, respond promptly to individual needs and provide personalized customer engagement and in-depth product explanations, just like our top salespeople. In the first quarter of 2027, the first batch of mass-produced IRON robots will begin trial deployment in some XPeng stores.

I expect IRON to become one of our star employees, delivering a delightful experience to customers visiting our stores. In the second quarter of 2027, we will officially launch XPeng IRON for external commercial customers. As an advanced general-purpose humanoid robot, IRON can quickly learn and adapt to different tasks across a wide range of commercial scenarios, taking on different roles at different times based on needs 24/7. As IRON deliveries scale up, large volumes of high-precision data collected from real-world scenarios will substantially accelerate the iteration of our robotics AI models and further strengthen our technological leadership.

Over the past several months, as I have become more deeply involved in the technical deployment -- development and organizational management of our robotics business, my confidence in successfully deploying and developing advanced humanoid robots has grown steadily. On the business model, I'm optimistic that XPeng IRON has the potential to far surpass the most popular premium vehicle models on the market in terms of both sales potential and gross profit. At the upcoming XPeng AI Tech Day this month, I plan to share our technical perspectives on automobiles, robotics and the physical AI paradigm, along with some of the results achieved through real-world applications.

As large language model companies enter the robotics space, physical AI companies, in my view, will retain irreplaceable competitive advantages. Leveraging capabilities in hardware, mass production, data, edge computing power and commercial deployment, these companies can enable the safe, reliable and large-scale deployment of cars as robots and humanoid robots across countless real-world scenarios, unlocking tremendous productivity gains. At XPeng AI Tech Day and the Guangzhou Auto Show, the latest version of XPeng IRON will be showcased and will feature a range of distinctive capabilities. I look forward to sharing these exciting developments with you. As autonomous driving regulations ease globally and the competitive landscape evolves, international automakers and mobility companies face an increasingly urgent need for technological transformation.

In response, we officially launched our Technology Solutions business, XPeng AI Engineering, in October. We're opening up opportunities for collaboration with external partners in smart electric vehicle technologies while offering physical AI solutions spanning Turing AI chips, foundation models, autonomous driving and robotics. We have established a dedicated business development team that is already in discussions with multiple companies. Our goal is to bring XPeng's technologies into the global automotive, mobility and robotics ecosystem, fostering greater openness and shared success. For the fourth quarter of 2026, I expect deliveries to be approximately 169,000 to 174,000 units, representing year-over-year growth of 45.4% to 49.7%.

Total revenues are expected to be between RMB 30.4 billion and RMB 31.8 billion, up 36.6% to 42.9% year-over-year. I'm very confident that Q4 will set new records in both deliveries and revenue while continuing to improve the quality of our operations. Moreover, we'll enter the first quarter of 2027, a traditionally low season for the industry, with a substantial order backlog. Industry headwinds will further differentiate companies, and we aim to widen our lead over competitors through sustained growth momentum, abundant cash flow and healthy profit margins. Physical AI development is not a sprint, but a marathon over the next decade.

Looking ahead at 2027, I plan to devote more attention to enhancing our overall operational performance and strengthening our ability to generate cash. At the same time, we'll accelerate the mass production and delivery of advanced humanoid robots and substantially strengthen XPeng's local market presence and brand momentum worldwide. Over the coming quarters, you'll see the benefits of economies of scale increasingly translate into our better operating results with technology-driven revenue growth and cost optimization becoming more evident. Our innovations in AI infrastructure and the deployment of recursive self-improvement, or RSI, in autonomous driving have significantly improved our R&D productivity and operational efficiency.

This enables us to achieve far greater progress in R&D than before with comparable levels of human and computing resources. In the short to medium term, we aim to achieve positive cash flow and profitability for our automotive business, providing a solid financial foundation for our strategic investments in physical AI. XPeng's emerging physical AI businesses benefit from strong synergies with our automotive business, enabling highly efficient R&D investment while developing diversified revenue streams across both B2C and B2B markets. Ultimately, our strategic investments will build lasting competitive moats in technology, brand recognition and commercial ecosystem. Step-by-step, we'll move towards sustainable profitability as we pursue our vision of becoming a global leader in physical AI. Thank you, everyone.

With that, I'll now turn the call over to our VP of Finance, James, who will walk you through our financial performance for the third quarter of 2026.

Jiaming Wu: Thank you, Xiaopeng. Now let me provide a brief overview of our financial results for the third quarter of 2026. I'll reference RMB only in my discussion today, unless otherwise stated. Our total revenues were RMB 24.28 billion for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 19.1% year-over-year and an increase of 23% quarter-over-quarter. Revenues from vehicle sales were RMB 21.63 billion for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 19.8% year-over-year and an increase of 26.9% quarter-over-quarter. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher vehicle deliveries and higher average selling price as a result of the improvement in product mix of models.

Revenues from services and others were RMB 2.65 billion for the third quarter of 2026, representing an increase of 13.7% year-over-year and a decrease of 1.9% quarter-over-quarter. The year-over-year increase was primarily attributable to increased revenues from carbon credit trading. Gross margin was 18.9% for the third quarter of 2026 compared with 20.1% for the same period of 2025 and 20.7% for the second quarter of 2026. Vehicle margin was 13.1% for the third quarter of 2026 compared with 13.1% for the same period of 2025 and 12.1% for the second quarter of 2026. The quarter-over-quarter increase was due to the improvement in product mix of models.

R&D expenses were RMB 2.85 billion for the third quarter of 2026, representing an increase of 17.5% year-over-year and a decrease of 2.1% quarter-over-quarter. The year-over-year increase was mainly due to higher expenses related to development of new vehicle models and AI-related technologies as the company expanded its product portfolio to support future growth. SG&A expenses were RMB 2.78 billion for the third quarter of 2026, representing an increase of 11.4% year-over-year and an increase of 11.2% quarter-over-quarter. The year-over-year increase was primarily due to higher marketing and advertising expenses and higher personnel costs related to the sales functions. The quarter-over-quarter increase was primarily due to higher marketing and advertising expenses and higher commission to the franchise stores.

As a result of the foregoing, loss from operations was RMB 0.75 billion for the third quarter of 2026 compared with RMB 0.75 billion year-over-year and RMB 1.14 billion quarter-over-quarter. Net loss was RMB 0.87 billion for the third quarter of 2026 compared with net loss of RMB 0.38 billion year-over-year and net loss of RMB 1.34 billion quarter-over-quarter. As of September 30, 2026, our cash position was RMB 45.41 billion. To be mindful of the length of our earnings call, I would encourage listeners to refer to our earnings press release for more details on our third quarter 2026 financial results. This concludes our prepared remarks. We'll now open the call to questions. Operator, please go ahead.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Your first question comes from the line of Tim Hsiao with Morgan Stanley.

Tim Hsiao: [Interpreted] So my first question is about the 2027 outlook and growth. How do you see Chinese auto domestic and overseas sales growth in 2027? And which products and pricing segment will drive XPeng's growth? And what could help the company to buck the cyclical industry downturn and keep gaining market share? That's my first question.

He Xiaopeng: [Interpreted] First of all, thank you for the question. I think that in 2027, the domestic automotive industry will still face headwinds, but it's going to be slightly better than 2026. Now in terms of the overseas market opportunities, I think it will represent a very significant growth for XPeng, definitely a major and rapidly growing opportunity for us because this year, if you look at the total vehicles exported from China, they are mainly composed of a considerable proportion of ICE vehicles and hybrid vehicles. However, I have a firm belief that BEVs will actually excel in the future in 2027 and 2028.

Looking ahead to 2027, I think that XPeng will significantly outpace the industry's sustained growth because one of the most important factor is, first of all, to sell well and do well in the current models that we have in our current price segment. This year, we actually placed a lot of emphasis on particular models starting from, for example, GX and L05 and L03. We can actually see that 3 months or 6 months after they were launched, we already see very good results and market feedback in terms of the sales volume. And next year, in 2027, we are also going to launch new models and safer versions, thereby broadening our entire product portfolio.

Now knowledge -- international-wise, we also will expand and diversify our channels as well, not only internationally, but also domestically. For example, previously, we mainly prioritized top-tier cities in China. However, we believe that we can actually deepen our distribution to lower-tier cities, for example, in the Northern -- Northwest and also western part of the domestic market, which will allow us to basically build our differentiated factor to improve conversion efficiency among our customers. At the same time, as we just mentioned, the overseas market will be a huge driving force for us. The growth rate will also increase at least by double next year. I'm hoping for actually a lot of growth in our domestic and international market.

Next year, I think it's going to represent basically the first year of our rapid growth for XPeng no matter if you look at the product capabilities and also our profitability and autonomous driving capability.

Tim Hsiao: [Interpreted] My second question is about the humanoid robots. As more LLM heavyweights enter physical AI, where will the XPeng robotics moat lie? Is that going to be models, data, motion control, hardware or faster deployment at scale? Does that heavy investment in proprietary model still makes economic sense for a company like XPeng? That's my second question.

He Xiaopeng: [Interpreted] Thank you. This is a very interesting question. Actually, it has been the subject of extensive discussion recently, including our internal discussions within our own company. Now regarding this topic, I actually would like to draw everyone's attention back to, for example, back in 2015 to 2020, around that time, that's when the R&D of autonomous driving first started. We actually already saw many people achieving autonomous driving through a computer simulation. However, you can actually see them failing to be deployed in the real world due to lack of precision and deployment capabilities. Also, there is issues regarding the downstream security as well.

We also saw that back then, I remember it was around 2018 when there were a lot of L4 companies made a lot of great demonstrations. But today, there isn't really a lot of their rollout on the road as expected. So there was a lot of actual deployment issue as well. Sometimes it has to do with their cost structure. There were also at a time when the market was prevalent with a lot of combination of cloud and edge architecture. But actually, today, you don't see them deploying on the road. The most critical issue is latency.

So what I'm trying to convey here is, first of all, based on our assessment, it's very, very difficult to try to use a general model or a System 2 model to achieve the combined capability of System 0, 1 and 2. It's actually very, very difficult to deploy it using traditional routes. So different companies now are working on different robots. I think they will actually present different competitive moat. And for XPeng as our company, we need to focus on 4 capabilities or 4 directions of development. And the first one is actually our hardware capability. Now a lot of people when they talk about physical AI, they thought that the emphasis is on AI.

No, the emphasis should be on physics. So the physical capability is very important. And the second factor is large-scale commercial production or mass produced -- production capability. Now when we, XPeng, entered the space, we come with our manufacturing capability and our sales capability, which will be very, very useful in the future physical AI day and age. And the third area is basically the data capabilities with scale. Right now, I actually see that many companies are spending a lot of money to purchase high-quality, diverse data, especially on visual data.

For example, when it comes to physical AI, it's just like when it comes to the functions of a human being, it's very important that we have, for example, the touch feedback, the pressure, the temperature, haptic data, et cetera, tactile sensation. These are very, very critical to having physical AI capability. And the fact that we actually have a lot of visual data is very, very competitive in the market. With hardware and real-world data feedback, it would make physical AI more possible. Obviously, the true generalization and deployment of physical AI ultimately depend on the computing power, not only in the cloud, but also at the edge as well.

So we're going to see that inference at the edge and also cloud-based training, cloud-based simulation, all requiring massive computing power support on different fronts. In this regard, I believe that Chinese EV companies with in-house development capability have actually a strong moat compared to international players. And that is basically my take on the -- on your question. Thank you.

Operator: The next question comes from the line of Tina Hou with Goldman Sachs.

Tina Hou: [Interpreted] My first question is regarding the 2027 overseas sales target, which is at least doubling from 2026. So among this, could you give us some color on different geographic distribution and also on the new model pipeline in overseas market as well as how do you plan to do a combination of pricing, spec and smart capabilities to raise your market share in overseas market?

Gui Hongdi: Tina, it's Brian. Let me answer your question here. First of all, yes, we're very excited about the overseas opportunity. As Xiao He mentioned, next year, we aim to more than double what we achieved in terms of volume this year. And I think it comes from a number of factors. From geographic split, I would say Europe is still going to be probably around 50% or more of our volume. And then I think followed by Southeast Asia and Asia Pacific, probably around 30%. And then the rest will be the Middle East and Latin America, about 20%. So for us, we look at these markets, we think the growth will come from some of the recently launched models.

For example, we actually launched the G9L, the L05, the GX, all going to be global models next year. Some of those models, for example, even L03 when it's launched, I think only have about less than a quarter of deliveries this year. So you can see that most of the volume growth will be driven by these newly launched, I would say, global products. And also, our products covers, I would say, a pretty complete market segments from the more family mass market focus, we will have the L03, the L05 and G6 covering the mainstream family-use SUV market.

And for the high-end family used SUV, the G9 and G9L as well as the GX for select Middle Eastern markets will be also launched to cover the high-end users. And also our X9 is still one of the most popular MPVs in Southeast Asia. And increasingly, we're also launching in Europe as well. So I think given these new product launches, I think we have a lot of confidence of significant volume and share gains. And also in terms of channels and market development, we also continue to push on some of the high-potential markets. For example, I recently came back from Australia and also U.K.

I think these markets, we are now doubling down our commitment and investment in these markets. And we think the channel development will ensure strong market share growth in these key overseas markets. So internationally, we are looking to build our channel in terms of sales and service points to be more than 1,000. And also, I think in addition to the markets that we -- I mentioned in the U.K. and Australia, we also continue to develop core markets in Europe, core markets in Southeast Asia as well as in Middle East.

And then another thing, I think we're very, very, I would say, happy to see is that XPeng's brand positioning in global markets actually has been really differentiated from a lot of other Chinese EV brands. We are really viewed as tech-centric with a premium positioning, especially till next year, we are -- we would like to introduce our high-end ADAS skills, the NGP in European markets as well as other technology features. I think the continued leadership in tech differentiation will actually help us differentiate our brand positioning, also allow us to achieve premium pricing and premium product perception as well.

One -- the last point I want to make is that internationally, there's a lot of talks about potential trade barriers and tariff. I think as a company, we have been dealing with that already for a few years. We'll continue to be very nimble in terms of our product positioning, our pricing strategy as well as our channel business models. In addition, we also have been looking at the earlier deployment of manufacturing investments, for example, in Europe, in Southeast Asia and other markets where we think through localization, through build-out of local capabilities and scale-based cost reductions can actually allow us to be more competitive in these international markets. So overall, we're very excited about the growth.

And also, we think that the volume growth will bring us significant profitability as well.

Tina Hou: [Interpreted] My second question is regarding the gross margin as well as unit net profit for the overseas vehicle sales. And also, how do you plan to deal with the next year's export tax rebate decline? Which measures are you planning to take in order to kind of mitigate the impact on that?

Jiaming Wu: Tina, this is James. I would address your question here. So first of all, in the third quarter, our export volume has already exceeded 20% of our total volume. From a revenue perspective, obviously, it's even higher. We would expect the Q4 export portion to be at a similar level and obviously continue to expand over time. From a gross margin of our ex-business -- export business perspective, it is, I would say, more than double versus our domestic business from a gross margin perspective. But if you look into contribution margin on net profit level, the export business is even much more healthier into the several multiples versus the domestic business, partially due to its sales structure difference.

So for example, in certain markets, we operate under a distributorship model where our gross margin effectively is our net profit. So overall, we believe our export business margin is among the top tier in the industry. And I think XPeng is -- XPeng brand is very well positioned overseas with a price premium. And our goal in 2027 is obviously to continue to grow overseas market with more than double the volume versus 2026 and supporting a better operating performance for the group in the coming years. Now with regard to the tax policy evolvement, these are just normal course of business. And there are several actions that we are considering to take to counter that impact.

One of that is to accelerate our overseas localization effort to not only achieve a better scale, but also counter the tax rebate scheme changes. And that scheme is obviously related to the CBU exports versus parts and KD exports. So accelerating overseas localization is something that should help us overcome that impact. The other thing we can do is on the pricing side for pretty much all of the new products that we are pricing at the moment, already considering tax rebate changes into 2027. We are also planning on product cadence adjustments to cope with potential further tax rebate phasing out in 2028. So these are the actions we are considering.

And then lastly, I would say, from a scale perspective, next year, we expect to achieve higher scale with new products selling not only for a couple of months, but for the full year, including the new products that were launched in the second half of this year, including L03, L05, G9L and GX, which will subsequently supporting us to achieve scale as well as better profitability for our overseas market.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Ming-Hsun Lee with Bank of America.

Ming-Hsun Lee: [Interpreted] Looking for 2027, could you discuss your expectation for the gross margin trend? And also how will you reduce your loss and also the major cadence driver?

Jiaming Wu: Yes. Thanks. This is James. I will address your question. So first of all, I think it's still a little too early to provide 2027 earnings guidance. I think we'll provide more information in our next earnings call. If you look at our gross margin in the third quarter, there are a couple of things that are changing. One is our vehicle margin has improved quarter-over-quarter, driven by our better product mix, primarily due to the launch of GX, which accounts for almost 20% of our volume in the third quarter. Again, export volume increased from below 20% to more than 20%.

From a trend perspective, in Q4, given L05 delivery will start to commence and account for a bigger portion of our volume. So from an ASP perspective, we do expect a slightly lower ASP in the fourth quarter.

Gross margin is slightly sliding quarter-over-quarter versus Q2, and that's partially because of -- in Q2, if you remember, we have our technical R&D service revenue from our collaboration with Volkswagen and there was a major milestone achieved in the second quarter and lacking that driving slightly lower other revenue, but that's partially offset by higher carbon credit sales revenue that we start to recognize in Q3 and expect a similar level of carbon credit sales in Q4 because of our projected volume in Europe. So overall, we still expect our group margin in 2026 to be in the high teens. Okay? I would say in the 2027 from an outlook perspective, the overall scale is expected to grow.

Again, overseas volume will be more than double, better mix from overseas and better scale. From a challenge perspective, we've seen obviously continued challenge from a cost side due to AI-related memory chips and -- et cetera, export VAT refund, as mentioned earlier. There's also battery consumption tax that is being implemented, and we are in the process of discussing with our suppliers. But on the expense side, we would expect a relatively moderate growth in R&D expense versus 2026 and again, better efficiencies in the sales expense. So from a ratio perspective, as a percentage of revenue, both R&D and SG&A, we believe, will show a better trend in 2027.

And lastly, we expect commercial revenues to continue to commence and continue from our physical AI business. And it is going to be at scale and grow as our expectation. And the profitability of our robotics business, as Xiaopeng mentioned earlier, is expected to be meaningfully better versus, let's say, a premium EV in the market. So that's all we can share at this point. Thanks.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Xiaoyi Lei with Jefferies.

Xiaoyi Lei: [Interpreted] Congrats on the strong quarter. I just have one on humanoid robots. Your next-generation robot is heading into mass production by the year-end. How do you see demand over the next 1 to 2 years? And which kinds of companies and use cases do we expect to be the first buyers?

He Xiaopeng: [Interpreted] Thank you for the question. I think this is something that everyone in the space would like to go and explore. The issue is that today in China or even around the world, robotics as an industry is mainly towards the B2B side, even for larger businesses where they offer a lot of highly -- sorry, highly customized products. However, for us, we actually don't want our robots to require customization. Instead, we envision it as a highly standardized product for small to medium B2B customers and eventually for even individual household customers that doesn't need to be customized at all.

So when it comes to the entire business possibility or the business logic in the future, first, I think that if I were in Europe, I would say the best business sector to deploy robots right now is in industries. But I think the best scenarios for China is really in business and family. So for industrial robots, the requirements regarding safety may be slightly less stringent. However, the requirements for the hand's dexterity is slightly more demanding in terms of the capabilities and skills that you can have through this robot. And the criteria for cost is also more stringent as well.

However, in the context of commercial use and also for family household use, the emphasis is placed more on the safety and also the overall aesthetic appeal of the design of the robot. So the requirements are pretty much different depending on how and where you want to deploy your robots. And also, I think it's going to help us to build a great differentiation when we target different market segments. We believe that XPeng's robots may be different from many other products in the market. First, we aim for a highly human-like and versatile design.

And since our production line is deeply integrated into our in-house R&D and manufacturing production lines, I'm very confident about our manufacturing capability and also our supply chain capability, whereas other competitors in the market may face a lot of headwind in this regard. However, from my perspective, whoever in the market can be the -- whoever in the market is the first to develop high-quality robots both also with high safety features will be the one that actually wins in the market first because when it comes to the robot application and its generalized capability for use in commercial sense and also in household sense, it's very important to have high quality together with high safety and reliability.

And that's why right now, currently, when you look at the robots that have been sold, a lot of them are left sitting in the warehouse and doing nothing because they are unable to meet high safety and quality standards. And that's also a challenge that we have to face, and we need to work to overcome it. Nevertheless, I'm very confident that by the end of this year, specifically starting mass production on January 1 next year, with deliveries beginning in the second quarter of next year, we will actually achieve high quality and greater safety than any other robots available in the industry.

I believe that once we've overcome that challenge, we will be able to actually grow at a very rapid pace, far surpassing the current production capacity and sales scale of the non so -- not so high-end robot models.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Pingyue Wu with CITIC Securities.

Pingyue Wu: [Interpreted] This is Pingyue Wu from CITIC Securities International. And my first question is, what is the process of our overseas localization in the strategic regions? And what percentage of vehicles will be locally produced next year?

Jiaming Wu: This is James. I think this question was touched already a little bit earlier, but I will briefly address again. So if you look at our overseas from a localization perspective, we have localization footprints in Europe as well as in Southeast Asia, particularly. So there are several manufacturing footprint, including contract manufacturing efforts that we have already established. Different areas would require different localization requirements and the calculations are different. We have already started exploring another step of deeper localization, including locally sourced parts with suppliers in all of these markets. So I think these discussions are ongoing.

Eventually, we will meet whatever the localization requirements from the local market in order to achieve the savings from a duties perspective as well as from the local subsidy benefit perspective. So I think overall, you can expect our overseas localization to be deeper going forward. And in the meantime, that would also help us to counter, as earlier mentioned, the CBU-related tax, VAT tax refund rebate that's phasing out in 2027 and 2028 with a deeper localization footprint overseas, that will help us to not only become more competitive from a cost perspective overseas, but also saving duty shortcomings from the tax benefits perspective.

Gui Hongdi: Yes. Let me just add. I think you know that we already have local manufacturing in, for example, Europe in a partnership with Magna in Austria. In Southeast Asia, we actually have also manufacturing in Malaysia and Indonesia. So we're looking at definitely expanding and deepening localization, also manufacturing deployment next year. The exact, obviously, markets are yet to be announced, so just stay tuned. But also, I would say that we are very focused on making sure that we can develop a scaled and cost-competitive overseas supply chain that give us the ability to not just produce but also meet the requirement for local sort of regulatory as well as to satisfy our local customer needs.

So I think all of that, I think, are the sort of the focus for us in terms of development and investments.

Pingyue Wu: [Interpreted] Thank you. My second question is that in October, the company announced plans to open up its smart vehicle technology to global partners, offering full ecosystem collaboration that spans from vehicle technologies to AI chips and foundation models. And could you share any updates on the eco openness and the rollout of these solutions also regarding our partnership with Volkswagen. How should we understand the announcement of expansion to overseas market?

Gui Hongdi: Yes. This is Brian again. First of all, I think the commercialization of our technology is a key priority for us. And the formation of this new AI engineering services practice, I think, is really taking in the experience and we received from the Volkswagen collaboration. I think throughout the collaboration, we have developed the ability to work with third parties, service third parties and also generate significant revenue from our technology stack. And I think just a few points I want to make. First of all, is that we're actually getting a lot of inbound requests to really work with us on various level of tech stacks.

Obviously, in addition to the EV and powertrain-related vehicle platform related, we also have seen significant interest in our sort of AI, physical AI core that we have developed, leveraging our chips, leveraging our model, training, AI infrastructure, et cetera. So I think there is a full stack of interest that we have received. So in order to address that, I think we have formed this new business unit, which actually I'm personally leading that effort.

So I think the goal is that we want to really focus on significant partnership opportunities in the sort of the platform areas as well as developing new categories that can leverage our sort of AI and the physical AI capabilities that we developed to more, I would say, more industry and more segments. That's our goal. So I would say this effort is just -- I think we just started making that effort as a new business. We obviously have currently already been working with Volkswagen on the existing projects. There's other additional collaborations that we are discussing with Volkswagen and also other partners.

I think as we deepen the development of that opportunity, I think we see significant opportunity generated starts next year. So that's something I think will leverage both the, I would say, OEM partnership relationship model, which I would say, demonstrated by the Volkswagen partnerships, but also, I would say, building upon our new physical AI technologies into products that actually can be partnered not just with the OEM, but also other segments of physical AI, embodied intelligence, robotics, Robotaxis, Robovans and other areas as well. So needless to say, we're very open to these discussions, and we're currently focusing on multiple high potential opportunities.

Alex Xie: Thank you once again for joining us today. If you have further questions, please feel free to contact XPeng's Investor Relations through the contact information provided on our website or the Piacente Financial Communications.

#3115. This tiny box gives your older tech smart home superpowers – and it’s only $69

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Home Assistant gets new equipment to battle planned obsolescence and abandoned cloud services.

Home Assistant is perhaps the most versatile smart home automation system of them all, thanks to the extreme customization power it offers. Today, a tiny, new box-shaped device is giving Home Assistant users a way to make their existing electronics smarter, rather than replacing them to keep up with the times.

Also: Ring’s new drone patrols your home to keep an eye on things

The Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 is a multi-purpose piece of hardware made by Nabu Casa, the company behind official Home Assistant hardware. The device brings together several connectivity options, including RS-232 serial for older TVs and other equipment, and the ability to connect older stereo systems and amplifiers to modern multi-room audio setups.

“The most sustainable device is the one you already own,” said Paulus Schoutsen, founder of Home Assistant and Nabu Casa. “No device should be left behind because it doesn’t have smart capabilities, or worst of all, its cloud services get turned off.

With the AUX-2, Home Assistant is joining the fight against planned obsolescence and abandoned cloud services.

Modern smart home systems have a major drawback: they exclude working electronics simply because they weren’t designed to integrate with today’s smart home platforms. This is the problem that the AUX-2 addresses.

Instead of buying a new stereo system with smart features, consumers can use the $69 AUX-2 to make the devices they already own smarter, more connected, and easier to control.

A single AUX-2 can control multiple devices, depending on how they’re connected and the interfaces they use. The device’s limit has more to do with the number of physical connections required.

Also: How I open-sourced my smart home – and ditched Google for Siri

The AUX-2 lets you connect two serial-controlled devices directly through the RS-232 ports. The USB port can act as an expansion for compatible adapters. You can place one AUX-2 on an entertainment center and connect an older stereo and TV, then use another AUX-2 elsewhere in your house for additional equipment with physical serial connections.

According to Home Assistant, with an AUX-2, you can control an old AV receiver without the original app, have an older TV respond to commands without relying on its manufacturer’s cloud servers, or integrate existing audio equipment into modern multiroom sound systems.

This way, consumers won’t need to trash a functional piece of equipment simply because the manufacturer stops supporting it.

Aside from RS-232 serial, the AUX-2 also supports Bluetooth, Z-Wave, USB, PoE, and Wi-Fi for connectivity.

#3114. Apple Launches New App to Study How People Use AI for Health

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Since 2019, when Apple first launched its Research app, the company has partnered with medical universities and institutions to run a range of health studies on hearing, heart health and movement, women’s health and, most recently, the Apple Health Study, which covers a wide variety of health areas.

On Sunday, Apple launched its latest study, and it comes with its own app: the Apple Health AI Study.

During a press briefing, Apple said the study aims to understand how people interact with conversational health AI tools. To do so, it will examine comprehension, response quality, the drivers of user trust and everyday health actions.

The goal? To inform the responsible design of health AI experiences for both Apple and the industry and to explore how health AI might help people prepare for doctor’s visits. Key questions the study aims to address include: Do users understand the information provided by health AI? Do they trust it? Is it helpful?

This is particularly relevant considering that one in three US adults use AI chatbots for health information.

Study data will not be used to train AI models, but it may inform Apple’s feature development.

To facilitate the study, Apple is partnering with OpenEvidence, an AI platform designed specifically for doctors. It generates answers using medical information from these partners: The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, National Comprehensive Cancer Network, Nature and Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews.

In the dedicated app, study participants can ask the AI their text-based health questions and then see answers with linked, peer-reviewed clinical citations. They can also choose to share their HealthKit data, including sleep, lab results, activity and resting heart rate, for more personalized answers.

HealthKit is Apple’s hub for health and fitness data collected on the iPhone and Apple Watch.

The Apple Health AI Usage Study is open to 200,000 participants. You must be in the US and age 21 or older to participate. An Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone (iPhone 15 Pro or later) running iOS 26 or later is also required.

Why an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone? According to Apple, the study app requires the processing capabilities of those iPhones, and it uses on-device Apple Foundation Models that are part of Apple Intelligence. These models provide access to any large language model. For example, as part of the study, these models are used to classify question categories.

Each participant is asked to participate for up to 12 months. During this time, they can ask questions about general health, specific symptoms, recovery from a procedure and their own uploaded health data, as examples.

In addition to a baseline survey, participants will receive monthly surveys and additional surveys specific to preparing for doctor’s visits.

Participants will also be prompted to check in with the app. For instance, if you have a paired Apple Watch, you will receive notifications to check in, along with suggested topics to explore.

If there is a complete lack of participation, a participant may potentially be removed from the study.

After downloading the Apple Health AI Study app, participants must complete a mandatory onboarding process that includes informed consent. They will also be asked to share their demographic information, such as race, age and education level, which will be used to explore how these factors may affect their preferences and communication needs. Then, they can start asking the AI questions.

The iPhone first processes questions using tools designed to remove details that could identify participants. They then go to a secure cloud-based study environment managed by a third-party study support contractor called UST Global, where queries are delinked from individual participant IDs and screened using tools designed to further remove any remaining personal details. Lastly, this info is sent to OpenEvidence, where answers are generated using supporting reference materials.

OpenEvidence will delete both question and response data within 24 hours.

A small group of Apple researchers will have access to coded versions of survey responses, separated from personally identifiable information, summaries of conversations and categories of the most common conversation types.

Within the study app, there are also safety guardrails that detect concerning questions and respond by suggesting that a participant follow up with a provider or other resources if needed.

There is no live monitoring, and study staff won’t contact participants if any questions related to self-harm are asked.

It’s also up to the participant whether they share any HealthKit metrics. They will first have to choose to upload their clinical health records to Apple’s Health app, and then separately choose to share those records from the Health app to the new Apple Health AI Study app.

The Apple Health AI Study app is now available in the App Store. As of now, there is no set publication date for the study.

#3113. The five things to look for when buying a home security camera

Home security cameras have become ordinary household hardware. SafeHome.org’s 2026 survey of 2,435 US adults found that 61% of households have at least one, up from 52% in 2024 and 42% in 2023, while video doorbells have reached 48% of households. Renters drove much of that growth. Their adoption rate jumped from 42% to 54% between 2024 and 2026, which makes sense given how many battery-powered cameras can be mounted without drilling and moved at the end of a lease.

In other words, when looking for one of the best home security cameras, it makes more sense to start with the features and subscription, rather than the headline numbers on the spec sheet. That, of course, can make finding the right one even harder. Here are some things to keep in mind when looking for a home security camera.

Arlo's Essential Wireless Security Camera helps you keep an eye on all the places that matter most. With Smart Detection for people, pets and packages, along with real-time alerts and color night vision, this high-quality security camera will give you peace of mind. Get two wire-free, rechargeable cameras this Black Friday, and with easy installation, they'll be up and running for the holidays.

The best way to figure out what security camera is right for you is to start with thinking about what you actually need a camera for.

A video doorbell suits packages and callers because its head-to-toe view and two-way talk are built around a front door. A driveway or yard needs a weatherproof outdoor camera, while a floodlight camera covers a broader area and adds deterrence. As a rule, cover each entry point instead of asking one camera to watch the entire property.

Prices generally fall into three useful bands. Budget models can be found for as little as $29, but you can still find features like 2K video and a pan-and-tilt designs that physically turn to cover a room. Mid-range models (around $100) offer good value, with additional features or better designs. Premium hardware reaches the $249 level and beyond, where you'll find such things as 4K video.

The number of megapixels figure on the box matters less than how many pixels land on a face. A 4-megapixel camera with a 2,560-pixel-wide image and an 80-degree lens can, under the older IEC 62676-4 identification guideline, identify someone at roughly 20 feet. A 4K camera captures 3,840 pixels across, but pair it with a wider 100-degree lens and that estimate rises only to about 21 feet. The extra pixels have been spent on width, so with the same lens, 4K gives you roughly twice the identification distance of 1080p, not four times.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Treat these numbers as geometry rather than guarantees, especially since the IEC standard for measuring detail at distance was revised in 2025. It uses 500 pixels per meter of scene width for validating a known person and 1,500 for high-certainty identification, while many spec sheets still rely on the older 250-pixel guideline. For a doorbell, 1080p is generally enough because visitors are close. For outdoor cameras, 2K, usually around 2,560 pixels across, is the sensible default. Pay for 4K when you need more detail at distance rather than simply a wider view, and check that your storage and Wi-Fi can handle it.

That said, two ordinary cameras in the right places will often beat one expensive 4K model covering everything badly.

“Spend less time chasing the highest resolution number in isolation. More detail can be useful, but placement, nighttime visibility, and useful notifications deserve just as much attention,” says Lars Felber, director of PR at Eve Systems. “A camera pointed at the wrong part of the porch can miss what matters regardless of its resolution.”

Judge a camera on its night footage, too. Infrared night vision uses light outside the visible spectrum to produce a black-and-white image in darkness, so it can show details relatively cleanly, but not with any color. Color night vision needs ambient light from a streetlamp or porch, or a built-in light — though often color night vision is a little less detailed, and usually can't see as far.

Watch for smeared movement too, since some battery cameras reduce their frame rate at night. Keep the lens away from glass and nearby eaves, which can bounce infrared light back into it.

Power decides where a camera can go and whether it can record continuously. Battery models are the easiest to install and the most renter-friendly, but they sleep until motion wakes them, so you get event clips rather than a full timeline and may lose the moments just before a trigger. Plug-in models remove charging breaks but leave you with a cable to route. Hardwired doorbells and floodlights can support 24/7 recording.

Power over Ethernet, usually shortened to PoE, carries power and data down one network cable for a more dependable connection. PoE requires cabling and a compatible switch or recorder, which is more work than most people want for a single doorbell. Solar models are the compromise. Solar models still have a battery, but solar panels keep the battery topped up so you don't need to worry about manual charging.

A solar panel is often the more practical upgrade for an awkward outdoor mount. Just about every company that makes one of the best outdoor security cameras offers a compatible panel. You’ll need a position with dependable sun, and short winter days can still leave the camera reliant on its battery, though it still beats climbing a ladder every few weeks.

Outdoor hardware also needs a weather rating. IP65, which means dust-tight and protected against low-pressure water jets, is a common floor for outdoor cameras and suits eave-mounted units, while IP66 is the better target for fully exposed walls. Check the stated operating temperature too. Arlo rates the Pro 6 down to −4°F, while cheaper models don’t always cope as well with freezing conditions. If you live somewhere that gets truly cold, like Canada, many models may not work for you.

Before drilling, test Wi-Fi at the exact mount point with your phone. Exterior walls and foil-backed insulation can badly weaken 5GHz Wi-Fi, which is fast but relatively short-ranged. Many budget cameras use only 2.4GHz, which reaches farther but contends with more household congestion.

Finally, check your upload speed if you plan to run several cloud cameras. Local recording to a memory card or hub doesn’t use that upload link, but continuous cloud video can saturate it surprisingly quickly.

Often, the price you pay for the camera itself is just a starting point. You still have to store video — and unless you can do so locally, you may have to pay for a subscription.

A local hub splits the difference. These live in your house, but are connected to your cameras wirelessly, so footage can survive both a damaged camera and an internet outage. A hybrid setup is generally the better choice, with local recording for continuity and cloud copies for important events.

“One of the most important things to look for in a home security camera is if a subscription is required to set up and use the device,” says Carney. “Going into the purchasing process, consumers should be aware that some security companies tack on a required subscription as a hidden cost without being transparent about it at purchase.”

Without a plan, some company's cameras will only let you view live events, and not save recordings, or access all of a camera's features. Be sure to look at the price of the subscription, and see if what's being offered is worth the long-term investment.

Once footage is being recorded, the next problem is getting alerted only when it matters. A camera that pings every time a car passes will eventually be ignored. Custom motion zones, sensible sensitivity controls and reliable person, vehicle and package detection do more for daily use than another AI label. At a door, two-way audio is worth having too, so you can speak to a courier without opening it.

“A camera can be very advanced and still fail at its only job if notifications are delayed,” says Rod Sides, founder of Loxx Boxx. “Worse, if it displays too many notifications in a way that you haven’t customized, you’re more likely to overlook the one important notification that may pop up.”

And don’t forget the microphone, since many cameras record audio by default. Recording a private conversation without everyone’s consent can break the law in all-party consent states such as California. If you don’t need sound or two-way talk, switching it off is the safer default.

“What consumers can spend less time worrying about is having the highest resolution or every bell and whistle on the market,” says Zavin. “Instead, focus on what the camera can actually do when a potential threat arises.”

For most homes, a well-placed 2K camera with accurate detection and a local fallback is the better buy. Step up to 4K or paid AI search if you have a specific use for them, not just because they're available.

Christian de Looper is a freelance writer who has covered every facet of consumer tech, including mobile, audio, home theater, computing, gaming, and even car tech. #3112. If the November Windows update fails to install on your PC, here’s what to do

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Windows > Windows 11

This month’s security update is failing on some systems already running the preview update released in October. But there is a fix afoot.

Ah, Microsoft. Another Windows update, another glitch. This latest one affects some Windows 11 users who attempt to install this week’s November Patch Tuesday update, only for it to fail. But don’t worry, there’s already a fix in play.

Also: You can now restore Windows 11 even if it can’t boot up – here’s how

On its support page to the November update designated KB5132061, Microsoft revealed and explained this latest problem.

Windows users who installed the November preview update released on October 28 may run into a glitch when trying to install the actual November update released on November 10. In this case, the installation may fail to complete. Your PC might repeatedly try to install the update or you may simply see an error code such as 0x80070306, 0x800f0989, or 0x800f0993.

I can confirm the problem. I installed the preview update on one of my Windows 11 virtual machines. Trying to then install the actual November update triggered the installation error.

If you’re in the same boat, what can you do to fix this dilemma? Just be patient.

Also: Windows finally gets a built-in internet speed test tool – how to try it

Microsoft promises that all affected PCs should receive repairs within 24 to 48 hours starting from November 11, 1pm ET. For this, make sure your PC is connected to the internet and is set up to receive updates via Windows Update. Head to Settings and select Windows Update. You may already find the November update known as 2026-11 Security Update (KB5132061) (26300.9974) available again. If so, select it to install it, and the process should work now.

I tried this on my virtual machine, and the November update installed without a hitch. But if you still bump into errors, check out Microsoft’s support page on troubleshooting problems updating Windows.

Microsoft typically releases each monthly Windows update in two phases.

First, there’s an optional preview update that kicks off around the end of the previous month. This one is considered a non-security update because it contains only feature changes. In this case, the preview update for November was released on October 28. Labeled KB5127936, this one unveiled the new customizable right-click menu, Cloud rebuild option, and other feature changes.

Also: You can change Windows settings directly from a search now

Second, there’s the actual mandatory Patch Tuesday update that contains both security patches and the non-security changes. Here, the November KB5132061 update was rolled out on November 10.

The preview updates are designed for IT administrators, software testers, and others who want an early look. That means they aren’t always fully baked and may contain a few bugs. But since they pop up in Windows Update, anyone can install them.

The actual Patch Tuesday updates are for all Windows users. In this case, there seemed to be an incompatibility or other conflict between the two updates that Microsoft then had to resolve.

#3111. Mercedes’ New Point-to-Point Driver Assist Helped Me Overcome My Fear of Driving

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

New hands-free highway and driving-assistance features are coming to select US models next year. I got an early look at the tech to see if it could make me feel more comfortable behind the wheel.

“This can go one of two ways,” I think as I slide behind the wheel. “Either this makes city driving a lot less intimidating, or I regret ever giving it a try.”

As someone who rarely drives – and doesn’t even own a car – in San Francisco, I was eager to see whether Mercedes-Benz’s new point-to-point driving assistance system could ease my anxiety as I navigated the city’s notoriously challenging streets. How would it handle the many four-way stops, steep inclines, pedestrians, cyclists and double-parked robotaxis?

After an hour of weaving through these complex environments, I walked away feeling more at ease than when I started. That’s largely because I barely had to lift a finger – or a foot.

I got an early opportunity to try Mercedes-Benz’s new point-to-point driver assistance system, MB.Drive Assist Pro, which will roll out to select California customers in December before expanding to the rest of the US next year. The Level 2 system handles functions like steering, braking and acceleration, but the driver has to be attentive and ready to take over at any moment. However, I hardly ever needed to.

As I made my way through San Francisco’s Financial District, Marina and North Beach in a Mercedes-Benz GLC 400, I repeatedly had to resist the urge to tap the brakes, press the accelerator or grab the steering wheel out of instinct. But within minutes, my apprehension had given way to awe at just how much the system could handle and how little I needed to do. With MB.Drive Assist Pro engaged, I watched as the vehicle obeyed traffic signals, yielded the right of way and even maneuvered around stalled robotaxis. Occasionally, I had to briefly place my hands on the wheel so it would know I was paying attention, but I didn’t find it bothersome at all.

There were moments when I had to take control. At one intersection, a pedestrian was preparing to cross, but the system persisted in making a right turn. (The death glare I got was a sign I needed to take over and tap the brakes.) Further down the road, I grabbed the wheel to steer around a parked truck unloading cargo. Other times, my patience was tested as the car came to a complete stop at every stop sign (rolling stops are my forte, sorry not sorry). To its credit, though, the vehicle subtly asserted itself at four-way stops by inching forward as we waited for our turn.

Unlike Level 4 robotaxi services like Waymo and Zoox, Level 2 systems like MB.Drive Assist Pro aren’t fully autonomous, but can take some of the stress out of everyday driving, particularly in dense urban environments.

Tesla’s so-called Full Self-Driving (Supervised) offers similar capabilities, navigating city streets, maneuvering around obstacles, making turns, changing lanes and responding to traffic signals, while still requiring driver supervision. Other systems like GM’s Super Cruise, Ford BlueCruise and BMW Highway Assistant offer hands-free driving on compatible roads, but are primarily designed for use on highways rather than complex city streets.

A feature like MB.Drive Assist Pro could not only bring increasingly advanced driver assistance technology to more car owners but also lay the groundwork for a future in which autonomous driving becomes more common in personally owned vehicles.

“We’ve clearly shown that the autonomous driving sector is an area that we will continue to develop and [be] involved in, and being one of the first companies to offer a system like you guys experienced today shows that we’re committed to be in that space and continue to grow,” Jason Hoff, CEO of Mercedes-Benz North America, said during a reporter roundtable following the demos.

MB.Drive Assist Pro uses 27 sensing components, including 10 cameras, five radar sensors and 12 ultrasonic sensors scattered throughout the vehicle. This hardware is currently available on certain 2027 Mercedes vehicles, including CLA Electric, GLE, GLS and S-Class cars. Starting with 2028 models, the company says more of its US passenger vehicles will be equipped to support the new feature.

Nvidia’s Alpamayo Stack powers the vehicle’s autonomous driving capabilities, using AI to interpret complex road scenarios and reason through driving decisions. It works alongside Nvidia’s Halos safety tech, including Halos OS, which provides safety guardrails to help ensure the vehicle follows the rules of the road, like stopping at a red light or waiting for an intersection to clear before crossing.

With Level 2 driving, there’s a mental hurdle that drivers like me will need to overcome and a certain degree of control we’ll have to relinquish to let the system do its thing. For instance, I sometimes found myself getting nervous as the car confidently moved into the oncoming lane to pass a stalled vehicle, even with approaching traffic. I was assured by the Mercedes team that the system can determine whether there’s enough room to safely squeeze through and otherwise wouldn’t attempt the move. Still, it’s not something I’d personally feel comfortable doing if I were in full control.

Some of this simply comes down to a learning curve. Over the hour I spent behind the wheel, I found myself feeling less anxious and more trusting of the system. I’d imagine that confidence would only grow with repeated use of MB.Drive Assist Pro, so drivers can feel less apprehensive about the car taking the lead, even if some decisions still occasionally give them pause.

MB.Drive Assist Pro will be available nationwide starting next year, with one-month, one-year and three-year subscription options. It’ll come to eligible Mercedes-Benz models including the 2026 CLA electric sedan, 2027 CLA sedan, 2027 GLC electric SUV, 2027 GLE SUV and coupe, 2027 GLS SUV and 2027 S-Class sedan. The system launched in China alongside the new CLA in late 2025. The upcoming rollout will bring it to the US and Germany as well.

Customers can factory-order MB.Drive Assist Pro, or purchase it digitally through the Mercedes-Benz store; it will be delivered as an over-the-air update. Mercedes hasn’t yet shared pricing.

Mercedes is also bringing hands-free highway driving to the US in spring 2027. I had the chance to try out that tech early as well, which proved to be an even bigger test of my trust.

As I drove from Alameda, across the Bay from San Francisco, onto Interstate 880 in a GLS 580, I took a deep breath and prepared to hand over some control to the car. After pressing the Resume button on the steering wheel (or adjusting the cruise control speed), I could activate Hands-Free Highway Assist. The feature comes with a few restrictions: you have to be on a freeway, not in an exit lane and away from construction zones or particularly sharp curves. You also can’t be driving faster than 85 mph.

Hands-Free Highway Assist lets you kick back a bit as the vehicle drives, slowing down and speeding up with traffic. A capability called Proactive Lane Change Assist can automatically switch lanes to overtake a slower vehicle or approach an upcoming exit based on the navigation route.

As with MB.Drive Assist Pro, you have to watch the road and be ready to take over at any time while using Hands-Free Highway Assist. Given the high stakes and high speeds, I wasn’t as hands-off with the highway driving feature as I was in the urban environment. Driving on the highway already feels nerve-wracking to me even when I’m in full control, so I couldn’t quite overcome the mental hurdle of letting go, physically and metaphorically, for more than about a minute at a time. I’d activate the feature, panic, then reactivate it. (Clearly, I’m a huge thrill seeker.)

One key hurdle is that it can be difficult to know when Hands-Free Highway Assist has been activated. An icon appears on the dashboard showing a green steering wheel with gray hands and two As on each side when the feature is available. Those hands will disappear when the feature is active, leaving only the green steering wheel and As. The icon turns red when you need to take over. Still, it was a little tricky to tell when the feature had correctly been enabled and when I hadn’t yet met all the requirements. Again, part of this is the learning curve, but it’s a big lesson to learn at 65 mph.

Still, when I was brave enough to activate the feature, it was impressive to witness the vehicle smoothly weaving across lanes on its own and following the flow of traffic, especially when I had the chance to try it again later in the afternoon on the S 580E. It seems like a handy capability that can make long-haul journeys and daily commutes a little less miserable.

Hands-Free Highway Assist will be available in the US in the spring, and pricing has yet to be determined. An early access program will give select California customers the chance to access the feature next month, alongside MB.Drive Assist Pro. Hands-Free Highway Assist will be on vehicles that support MB.OS (Mercedes’ in-house operating system) as part of the MB.Drive Assist offering, which already includes Steering Assist, Lane Change Assist and Proactive Lane Change Assist. The new feature will arrive via an over-the-air update.

After a day of stepping outside my comfort zone in more ways than one, it was fascinating to get a glimpse of where automotive technology is headed – and how it could make everyday drives, even the more stressful ones, feel a little less daunting. But for now, I hopped into an Uber and returned to my usual routine of avoiding the driver’s seat.

#3110. Why Turning Point Brands Stock Got Socked Today

The company filed a shelf registration statement early that morning.

Investors were turning away from Turning Point Brands (TPB -10.59%) on Monday, punishing the company's stock with a sell-off that lowered its stock price by almost 11%. This was in the wake of a regulatory filing revealing the tobacco specialist will seek new financing before long.

Before market open, Turning Point filed a mixed shelf registration form with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). This is a document in which a company, or some of its existing investors, registers a variety of its securities for sale with the intent to raise fresh capital or debt financing.

In Turning Point's case, it's registering its common and preferred stock, depositary shares, warrants, units (combinations of stock and warrants), and unspecified debt securities.

Currently, the company has 190 million shares of authorized common stock, and 40 million shares of preferred stock. The current count of common shares outstanding is under 20 million, meaning the company has over 170 million it could potentially sell.

In its filing, Turning Point wrote that it aims to use any proceeds raised from these securities "for general corporate purposes, including working capital, repayment of indebtedness, acquisitions and other business purposes."

The company added that it could opt to invest in interest-bearing securities, such as bonds, until the proceeds are applied for the mentioned purposes.

Shelf registrations usually ding investor morale, as existing shareholders worry about stock dilution, increased debt levels, or both. In short, they're taken to mean that a company has gotten into a situation where it needs a cash infusion to support itself.

These documents are fairly vague, so we don't yet have any idea of how large Turning Point's fundraising efforts will be. So I wouldn't buy or sell the company's stock purely on that basis. But considering the company's recent struggles, I'd be inclined to avoid its equity regardless.

Robert Pattinson is staying booked and busy.

It’s safe to say Robert Pattinson is on a generational run, starring in The Odyssey, The Drama, Die My Love and Primetime just this year alone. Having previously played Edward Cullen in The Twilight Saga and Bruce Wayne in Matt Reeves’ The Batman (and gearing up for a role in Dune: Part Three this December), he’s no stranger to major film franchises.

Now he’s adding one more major role to his portfolio: James Bond.

Amazon MGM Studios named the English actor the new 007 on Monday, ending the hunt to replace Daniel Craig, who played Bond from 2006 to 2021 in five films: Casino Royale, Quantum of Solace, Skyfall, Spectre and No Time to Die.

Several other British A-list actors were speculated to be in the running for the role, including Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor, but it seems Amazon MGM Studios is banking on a big-name actor with a proven record of box-office success for its lead. Pattinson’s connection to director Denis Villeneuve, who was also director of the Dune trilogy, likely played a role in the decision, too.

“To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement,” Pattinson said in a statement. “I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

Read more: Ready to Watch a James Bond Movie? These Are My Top Recommendations for You

Pattinson is the eighth actor to play James Bond on screen. The full list of actors who have portrayed 007 includes Sean Connery (1962-1983), David Niven for one (unofficial) film in 1967, George Lazenby for one film in 1969, Roger Moore (1973-1985), Timothy Dalton (1987-1989), Pierce Brosnan (1995-2002) and Craig (2006-2021).

The next Bond film has not yet been titled and is not expected to begin filming until 2027, with a 2028 release date. Steven Knight (Peaky Blinders) has been brought on as the screenwriter, with Amy Pascal (Project Hail Mary) and David Heyman (Harry Potter series) producing and Tanya Lapointe (Dune trilogy) executive producing.

Amazon formally closed its acquisition of MGM Studios in 2022 for $8.45 billion, giving it the rights to distribute all James Bond films. In 2025, Amazon MGM Studios announced a joint venture with longtime franchise producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli to remain co-owners of the franchise, while ultimately giving Amazon MGM Studios creative control.

“Few films carry the kind of anticipation that comes with James Bond, and we have strived to honor the passionate fans, the legacy and the future of this iconic character,” said Courtenay Valenti, head of film at Amazon MGM Studios. “We are thrilled to officially welcome Robert Pattinson as our 007 and are confident he will bring something truly special to this role. Robert, Denis, Amy, David and Tanya are embarking on an amazing adventure together.”

#3104. Google’s Pixel Tag tracker won’t work as well on older Android phones – check our list

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android

Several of the tracker’s best features require Bluetooth 6.0-compatible device.

Google’s Pixel Tag, the company’s take on an Android-exclusive Bluetooth tracker, is finally here, following its August announcement during the Google I/O developer conference.

Also: Google’s new Android XR glasses have lower ‘creep factor’ than competitors

Pixel Tag is a complete Bluetooth tracker for Android users that appears less confined to device-specific ecosystems than Samsung’s Smart Tag 3 and Apple’s AirTag.

However, if you look at Google’s footnotes, the Pixel Tag’s functionality is diminished when an older Android phone is involved. Several of the tracker’s best features require a compatible device running Android 9.0+ and Bluetooth 6.0+, according to Google.

Android 9 and newer encompasses a lot of devices, but Bluetooth 6.0 and newer doesn’t. Here’s what to check before you buy.

Smartphones began shipping with Bluetooth 6.0 in 2025, starting with the Samsung Galaxy S26 Plus and Galaxy S26 Ultra. The following phones also have Bluetooth 6.0:

If your Android phone is older than any of the listed above, even by a generation, it likely supports Bluetooth 5.3 or 5.4 — not enough for the Pixel Tag’s best features.

The Pixel Tag’s precision-finding capabilities are powered by Bluetooth Channel Sounding, a key feature introduced in Bluetooth 6.0. Nearly every review I’ve seen of the Pixel Tag, including our own, tests the tracker when paired with a Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 11, or Pixel 11 Pro.

I assume that Android users whose phones run Android 9.0+ but lack Bluetooth 6.0+ can use the Pixel Tag for very basic, general location tracking. These users may see the tracker’s general location, but Google’s device compatibility footnote appears several times throughout its press release.

The following features require Android 9.0+ and Bluetooth 6.0+, according to Google’s release:

So, on older Android devices without Android 9.0+ and Bluetooth 6.0+, the following aren’t supported: locating the exact direction and distance of your tracked devices, pinging a tracker when you don’t see it, or giving your tracked devices a custom name.

Also: 3 ways Bluetooth 7 upgrades your devices beyond lossless audio

Additionally, shorter-distance tracking requires an ultra-wideband chip inside your Android phone. Channel Sounding handles distance and direction at longer ranges, while UWB takes over for shorter ranges. Most premium Android phones with Bluetooth 6.0 also have UWB chips, but several of Google’s base-model phones lack a UWB chip.

Samsung’s base-model, A-series, and Z Flip-series phones also lack UWB, resulting in more phones that can’t access the Pixel Tag’s short-range precision finding capabilities.

With all the specs in mind, the Pixel Tag is the best option for users of recent premium flagship Android phones. Those without the latest Bluetooth connectivity will find that the Pixel Tag works like any other Bluetooth tracker, with basic functionality.

Also: These are the closest things to AirTags for Android users

The good thing is that a single Pixel Tag is $30, so it’s not much more expensive than a Tile Tag, and cheaper than a Chipolo Loop. Still, if your phone doesn’t support Bluetooth 6.0, you might be better off looking for a cheaper option until you’re ready to upgrade.
